title: Pattern Headings: Musical Compositions
scope: Free-floating subdivisions usable under headings for musical forms and types of compositions, medium of performance, style, function, music for special seasons or occasions, musical settings of special texts, and headings with the subdivisions –Hymns, –Music, –Musical settings, –Songs and music (not the general heading Music). Lists 1-3 are usable under headings for collections of musical works and individual works, specific form/genre headings, and Chamber music; Dramatic music; Instrumental music; Sacred vocal music; Vocal music.
general_notes: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.  Headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on the lists given here may be found in the subject authority file.

Use “, Arranged” as a free-floating qualifier with headings for arranged instrumental music (e.g., Piano music, Arranged). When use of “, Arranged” is permitted for vocal music, the heading incorporating it must be established. (sec. 2)
Basic order of subdivisions for musical compositions: geographic, chronological, topical, form. (sec. 7)
Do not use geographic subdivisions for collections of works by one composer. (sec. 3)
List 2 and List 3 note: Most form subdivisions coded $v in this list may also be used as topical subdivisions coded $x when assigned to works about the form (see H 1075, sec. 1.d.).
7 A change in policy occurred February 2024, which removed the limitations on the application of subdivisions from List 1.

entries.notes: Use only when chronological focus is stated or implied in the title or series statement. Do not use for jazz and popular music (H 1916.5), in headings for folk or non-Western music (H 1917), for collections of works by one composer, for individual musical works, or following the subdivisions –Hymns; –Music; –Musical settings; and –Songs and music.

[6] May be subdivided topically by a religion or Christian denomination. Editorially establish each heading of the type that is so subdivided, e.g., Popular music–Religious aspects–Islam; Popular music–Religious aspects–United Methodist Church. For instructions on the use of the subdivision, see H 1998.
